problem: flip() now returns closed unchanged, so complement() gives each gap the same edge closedness as the neighbouring interval and difference() puts removed endpoints back and drops kept ones (e.g. [0,10] minus [3,5] still contains 3 and 5; A minus A leaves points 0 and 10).
No tests cover difference()/complement() endpoint behaviour, which is how an edge-inverting regression in difference() landed unnoticed.

Pre-existing: validate_bounds only rejects a closed unbounded end when the bound is None, so a float('inf') or float('-inf') bound with a closed flag is accepted and exported as None with closed=True, which the module then refuses to parse back.
Pre-existing: is_number accepts NaN, and since every NaN comparison is false, is_empty, sort and merge silently give meaningless results.

Pre-existing: complement() passes the -inf end of its leading gap through flip() with prev_hc=False, so that gap comes out closed at -inf, which breaks the module's own rule that an unbounded end must be open; on main an open -inf on the left side cancels it out in the intersection, so it is harmless there.
Pre-existing: parse_all accepts any iterable, so a dict is silently read as its keys instead of raising the documented 'expected a sequence' error.
Pre-existing: is_number only catches TypeError, so a bound type whose comparison or addition raises another exception escapes parse() without being turned into the documented ValueError.
